chain_words.nuance: possible in principle, though not expected
capable of happening under some circumstances
more likely than not, on the available evidence
strongly expected to happen or to be the case
beyond reasonable doubt, with no room for error

explanation: These words all express degrees of likelihood, rising from something merely conceivable to something beyond doubt. In academic writing they mark how confidently a claim is put forward.

usage_notes.difference: 'Possible' only means something could happen, while 'probable' means the evidence makes it more likely than not, so it signals a stronger claim.
